rationale: The production roadmap requires Evidence Spine to aggregate freeze register items, bug ledger records, audit JSONL, screenshots and API responses with evidence_id, source, checksum and retention_policy. This change extends the public core EvidenceSpine API with a checksummed artifact registry and API endpoints while preserving the existing hash-chain append/query/verify contract. It is D3 because it changes a core public API and introduces a new persistent table used by audit and governance consumers.

steps: Revert artifact registry methods and EvidenceArtifact from core/evidence_spine.py.
Revert core.evidence_spine manifest event and lifecycle changes.
Revert artifact-specific tests in test_core_evidence_spine.py and test_api_integration.py.
Run the evidence spine, memory evidence store, signer v2, lifecycle gate and API integration tests twice.
Leave any existing evidence_artifacts rows inert; do not delete production audit data during rollback.

fidelity_test.description: Verify that Evidence Spine can register JSON and file artifacts, attach them to the hash chain, list/filter them, expose them through API routes and detect file checksum drift.
pre_conditions: Core EvidenceSpine is initialized with a clean SQLite database.
API integration tests run against the FastAPI app test client.
Temporary file artifact is available for checksum verification.
steps: Register a JSON artifact and verify evidence_id, checksum, retention_policy and chain_entry_id.
Register a file artifact, verify it succeeds, mutate the file and verify checksum_mismatch.
List artifacts by source and artifact_type.
Verify the existing Evidence Spine hash chain remains valid.
Register and verify a JSON artifact through /api/v1/core/evidence/artifacts/json.
Run the broad evidence/API test suite twice.
fidelity_test.expected_outcome: Artifacts have stable evidence_id values, sha256 checksums, retention policy metadata, chain links, API visibility and tamper detection for file-backed artifacts.
